comment: Sprint Workflow v0.2 routing policy. Declarative — runProvider still controls actual provider selection. Honored by /sprint:plan, /sprint:design, /sprint:execute, /sprint:release where a model class is needed (planning, review, scoping, judgment). No new SDK installs; routing intent is preserved by class even when provider-fallback.json drives an actual swap. v0.2 adds the `concurrency` block — advisory knobs for parallel-sprint lanes.

concurrency.rationale: Number of sprints that may execute concurrently before /sprint:execute halts new ones. v0.2 ships advisory-only — no hard cap yet. default_lane is the lane type assigned when /sprint:plan omits one. default_isolation is the recommended isolation type for non-default lanes (worktree reuses the builder/oneshot primitive).

enforcement.rationale: SP-20260514-002 soft-rollout — sprint-routing-guard hook emits warnings instead of blocking until 2026-05-21. After that, /warp:health raises a yellow advisory if mode is still 'warn'. Flip to 'block' once smoke confidence is high.

planning.rationale: Plan formation is the highest-leverage step. Strongest reasoning + diff-model review prevents fantasy plans.

plan_contract_review.rationale: Beta-like judgment over the Plan Contract — catches missing evidence, unsafe assumptions, scope creep.

design.rationale: PRD/STORIES/COPY/INPUTS/TRACE design benefits from a strong reasoner and a second-vendor read.

execution.rationale: Routine ticket execution is mechanical. Escalate to strong reasoning when a bugfix fails twice or a ticket touches architecture.

qa.rationale: 13-persona QA scan; diff review across two vendor families catches blind spots.

redteam.rationale: Adversarial reasoning is most effective when the redteam model is not the model that wrote the code.

retrospective.rationale: Synthesizes a post-sprint retrospective from tracker artifacts. Strong reasoning so the model can connect Plan Contract predictions to actual outcomes; diff_review catches hallucinated wins/misses by surfacing a second-vendor read before sign-off. Fail-open: synthesis failure auto-falls-back to skeleton retro (COPY C-7).

docs_sync.rationale: Docs/spec updates after code changes are mostly transcription — economical writer is fine.

tracker_updates.rationale: Status changes, link updates, checkpoint writes — structural work.

trace_updates.rationale: TRACE entry generation is structural, with a structured schema to fill.

external_service_setup.rationale: ESD records affect approval, billing, secrets. Strong reasoning + diff review prevents misclassification.

diff_review_rule: When diff_review is true, the sprint command MUST surface a second-model read from a different vendor row before the artifact is finalized. If a second vendor is unavailable, the command logs the unavailability (decision-ledger) and proceeds; it does not silently downgrade.
no_override_floor_note: Cheaper models never override these. Routing only chooses which model class drafts the artifact — the approval gate is a separate decision recorded in the approvals/ folder.
fallback_interaction: Sprint routing declares INTENT (a model class). Actual provider selection still flows through scripts/dispatch-agent.js / runProvider, which honors paths.providerFallbackPolicy. If the primary in a class is unavailable, runProvider falls back to a peer in the same class — routing intent (class) is preserved, vendor may shift.
notes: Sprint v0.1: this file is loaded by /sprint:* commands but provider selection is still done by runProvider. No new SDK installs.
Update procedure: edit this file, no schema bump needed for additive policy keys.
If you want to disable sprint routing in a downstream repo, delete this file — sprint commands fall back to a single 'use whatever runProvider picks' path and log the absence.
